stories.title: TD-067: sweep the 10 non-STOP alarm surfaces off brand --red-light (per Spool per-surface ruling)
stories.completionNotes: SWEPT 8 of 10 + the tier-aware refactor; the 2 --destructive surfaces DEFERRED per the story's own conditionalOutcome (no token gated -- see BELOW, this is the one AC not met). AMBER (Spool 'degraded is not danger'): #1 topbar down-glyph, #2 .tile[down] value, #4 .ltft-bar[down] value AND border (sweeping only the value would have left a red box around an amber number), #6 #dtc-clear-result[reset] (keeps font-weight:700 so it stays distinct from [blocked], which is also amber). CRITICAL-RED: #3 .ladder[data-stage=TRIGGER] border+banner -- terminal act-now SYSTEM state; earlier stages left amber so the escalation still escalates, and I asserted the banner COPY stays 'DRAINING - TRIGGER' in carousel.js, never the engine tier's 'PULL OVER' (--critical-red is now shared by two tiers, so the WORDS are what keep them apart). THE LOAD-BEARING ONE (#5): .detail-directive painted ONE blanket brand red for EVERY severity, which inverted the ramp TWICE -- a WATCH code's directive read REDDER than the --critical-red chip sitting beside it, and a MINOR gas-cap code got a red instruction it never earned. Now data-level-driven (stop->--critical-red, watch/unknown->--amber-warn, minor->--green-ok) over a NEUTRAL base, so an `na`/untagged row inherits no severity it doesn't have. CROSS-FILE CATCH, THIRD SPRINT RUNNING: the tier tag is applied in JS (renderDetailBody), so a CSS-only refactor leaves EVERY band on the neutral base -- no error, no styling, silently un-tiered. Tagged from view.level, the SAME tier the chip uses, so the two can never disagree; asserted in the JS source. NEW GUARD tests/ui/test_dashboard_alarm_tier_sweep.py (19 tests) imports the US-484-b suite's CSS parsers rather than re-implementing them (_ruleBlock's line-anchoring is load-bearing; a hand-copied weaker matcher would silently under-assert), strips comments before parsing (a prose token mention is not a declaration -- my own first scope-fence test tripped on this), and compares PARSED token references so drift in either file re-reds. Two guards make the deferral self-closing: the whole-file guard asserts the 2 #clear-confirm selectors are the ONLY brand-red rules left (debt can shrink, never silently grow), and a scope-fence asserts --destructive is declared/rendered in NEITHER file (cannot half-land as a guessed hex -- the exact drift US-484-a/b removed). Also pinned: no bare red HEX outside :root (inlining a literal is the same drift wearing a different hat). GREEN in-loop: 19 new pass; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 167 passed; ruff clean. GATES for PM: black+mypy not installed on the Windows host (standing gap); no config change so validate_config.py N/A. DEFERRED + ROUTED: #7 #clear-confirm .confirm-box + #8 #clear-confirm-ok need --destructive (Spool: MUST NOT be any alarm-red, MUST NOT be amber, different axis; Iris value + Atlas Rule-10 gate). Nothing in my inbox gated it, so I refused to guess. Inbox note filed for PM (2026-07-27-from-ralph-us488-destructive-token-gate-needed.md). TD-067 UPDATED, NOT CLOSED -- narrowed to those 2 lines. PASS/FAIL JUDGEMENT: marked passes:true on the strength of the conditionalOutcome (the PM-sanctioned partial), NOT because every AC is met -- the 'TD-067 closed' AC is explicitly unmet. Flip to false if you read strict pass/fail as overriding; the remaining work is exactly 2 declarations. PI-RUNTIME GATE OWED (the sweep intentionally changes what the panel looks like): DOWN/degraded/LTFT surfaces now read amber not red; ladder TRIGGER reads critical-red with earlier stages amber; a WATCH DTC detail's directive band must be AMBER (was red) and a STOP's must be --critical-red.

stories.title: Polish P-1: System Status card -- summary line + 2x2 grid + per-tile status dots (glanceability)
stories.completionNotes: ALL 4 ACs MET. THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL (say so first, it is the whole story): a summary line is a LOSSY COMPRESSION of four tiles, so it is precisely where a green-when-broken lie enters -- and the naive reading of AC-1 ('green ONLY when every source is genuinely good' => require all 4 == ok) produces the OPPOSITE dishonesty. DRIVE=IDLE is the only `neutral` this card emits and it means 'not recording', NOT 'broken'; requiring drive==ok would make green UNREACHABLE in the commonest state (key on, no drive started), so the line would read amber forever and the operator would learn to ignore it -- crying wolf. So I built THREE buckets, not two: ok=good; neutral=nominal-inactive (does NOT block green, is NOT an issue); unavailable=known-UNKNOWN (BLOCKS green -- never claim OK over a source we cannot read -- but is NOT an alarm, so it renders muted grey, not amber); amber/down=the only ISSUES. FAIL-CLOSED on vocabulary: an unrecognised level ranks as `unavailable`, never ok, so a tile level added in some future sprint cannot paint the card green by default (test pins it with a junk level). AC-1 TEXT: both of the AC's example forms render -- the LINE is the glanceable count ('SYSTEM · OK' / 'SYSTEM · 1 ISSUE' / 'SYSTEM · 2 ISSUES' / 'SYSTEM · 1 UNAVAILABLE') and the DETAIL names the worst source ('OBD LINK · RECONNECTING'), so the operator gets the count at a glance AND what to look at, without reading four tiles. Worst-wins, not first-wins; a real issue always outranks an unknown (an unreadable source can never mask a known fault). SSOT: summary is computed from the SAME tiles object the grid renders (test asserts view.summary == systemSummary(view.tiles)), so headline and grid can never disagree. AC-3 -- READ THIS BEFORE 'FIXING' THE DOT: the AC parenthetical says '(green/amber/red/neutral)' but the operative clause is 'MIRRORING the existing per-tile level', and after US-488/TD-067 swept `.tile[data-level=down] .tile-value` to amber there IS no red in this card's mapping. I implemented the MIRROR faithfully (down->amber) and did NOT invent a red dot: a red DOWN dot would re-open TD-067 one sprint after it closed AND would contradict the amber number sitting beside it. Test asserts dot and value resolve to the same token for `down`, so the two can never drift apart. AC-2: 2x2 via a new .sys-grid; all 4 tiles keep value AND detail (nothing dropped to make room). SCOPE FENCE (the trap): appendTile is SHARED with the idle card, battery card and LTFT card, so the dot is OPT-IN (3rd arg) -- defaulting it on would have restyled three shipped cards from a story scoped to one; also spelled out `.sys-grid .tile:last-child` explicitly because the base rule zeroes border-bottom there and the final grid cell would have rendered open-sided. CROSS-FILE CATCH, FOURTH SPRINT RUNNING: the grid/dot/summary are classes the JS must EMIT -- a CSS-only change styles markup that never renders, no error; guards assert the renderer emits each class, tags the summary with data-level, and appends the 4 tiles into `grid` and NOT into `body`. REAL BUG FOUND IN THE HARNESS (not my code): the node probe used subprocess text=True with no encoding, so Python decoded node's UTF-8 with the Windows locale codepage and turned the '·' separator into 'Â·' -- it failed as a one-char diff that looks exactly like a production string bug. Fixed in my file (encoding='utf-8'); the 5 sibling helpers share the omission but every one of their assertions is ASCII and passes today, so it is latent -- filed TD-068 rather than widening this diff. GREEN in-loop: 32 new tests pass; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 199 passed; ruff clean. GATES for PM: black+mypy not installed on this Windows host (standing gap); no config change so validate_config.py N/A; full suite is the PM integration gate (I touched no base module -- only the dashboard dist + one new test file). PI-RUNTIME GATE OWED (480x320): the card is deliberately re-laid-out -- confirm the 2x2 grid does not overflow at 480px with the longest tile values, the 17px summary line reads at a glance, and that a parked/OBD-off state shows a MUTED 'SYSTEM · 1 UNAVAILABLE' (not amber, not green).
acceptance: top SUMMARY line: 'SYSTEM · OK' (green) ONLY when every source is genuinely good; else the worst state ('SYSTEM · 1 ISSUE' amber / 'RECONNECTING' amber) -- honest-instrument F-1 (never green unless all-green)

stories.title: Polish P-2: context-aware system-setup menu access (⋮ parked-only + long-press always)
stories.completionNotes: ALL 4 ACs MET. THE JUDGEMENT CALL (state, note the reading): AC-1 says the ⋮ shows 'only on the parked/idle home CARD' but its own operative clause says it 'keys off the idle/live STATE the UI already consumes' -- and the goal is 'not reachable by a single accidental tap WHILE DRIVING'. I keyed it to the STATE, not to which card is on screen: while parked there is no driving-tap hazard, so hiding the ⋮ the moment the operator swipes off the idle card to System Status would cost the affordance for nothing. Every safety clause is satisfied by the state reading; the card reading only subtracts. FAIL-CLOSED, and this is the load-bearing pair: the unknown side of 'am I driving?' is the DANGEROUS side, so an absent/malformed/idle-less system-status hides the ⋮ (carouselIdle already fails closed to not-idle; I pinned it with junk levels incl. the truthy string 'true' and a bare {}). That is only safe BECAUSE the long-press is unconditional -- so I made the two paths one export returning BOTH flags, {tapVisible, longPress}, with a test asserting they DISAGREE while driving. If they ever collapse into one flag, either the tap comes back at 70mph or the override vanishes; either way that test re-reds. SSOT: reads the US-480-a `idle` boolean (Atlas idle-SSOT b), never re-derived from drive.state -- pinned in BOTH directions (drive='idle' + idle:false stays hidden; drive='recording' + idle:true shows), so a future 'helpful' fallback to the drive string re-reds. DEFENCE IN DEPTH for AC-4 ('never reachable by a single tap while driving'): CSS alone is one regression away from handing back a clickable target, so the click handler ALSO returns early on menuBtn.hidden -- `hidden` (the property, not a class) is deliberately the same rendered truth both the painter and the gate read, so they cannot disagree. Third layer: the button now ships hidden in dashboard.html, closing the pre-first-poll window when the context is genuinely unknown. CSS: stated `#menu-btn[hidden]{display:none}` explicitly rather than leaning on the UA sheet -- #topbar is a FLEX container, so any future `display` declaration on #menu-btn would outrank the UA [hidden] rule and silently restore the target. SCOPE FENCE (tested, not just intended): the long-press block must stay state-blind -- a guard slices the pointerdown..pointercancel source and asserts it contains no menuAccess/tapVisible/carouselIdle/menuBtn.hidden gating, because gating the override would lock the operator out in exactly the state where they may most need to stop a misbehaving service. AC-3 fences: requiresConfirm('stop') still true, powerwatch still restart-only, and Exit still routes through doAction (no direct postAction shortcut). WIRING (the recurring cross-file trap, FIFTH sprint running): a pure menuAccess() nobody calls passes every logic test while the ⋮ sits visible at speed -- guard asserts the poll tick calls updateMenuAccess(sysData), sharing the fetch updateIdleHome already made (no extra fetch, no second OBD touch). CAUGHT MID-FLIGHT: my own first tap-gate guard PASSED against the un-gated code -- the source slice ran on into openMenu/closeMenu and found THEIR `hidden` writes. Tightened the window to end at the next listener registration and confirmed it went red before implementing. A guard that cannot fail is worse than no guard. GREEN in-loop: 17 new pass; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 216 passed; ruff clean on the touched file (the 7 ruff I001s in tests/pm/ are pre-existing and out of scope). GATES for PM: `make` is not on this host's PATH (ran ruff directly); black+mypy not installed (standing gap); no config change so validate_config.py N/A; full suite is the PM integration gate (no base module touched -- dashboard dist + one new test file). PI-RUNTIME GATE OWED: parked -> ⋮ visible and opens on tap; start a drive -> ⋮ disappears within one poll and ONLY the 5s hold opens the menu; kill the state server -> ⋮ stays hidden and the hold still works. Minor cosmetic note for the CIO's eye: with the ⋮ removed from flow the version chip (margin-left:auto) now sits at the far right edge while driving -- intended, but confirm it reads right at 480px. CONDITIONAL OUTCOME RESOLVED (no Atlas gate): the story said route to Atlas only if the context-aware ⋮ touches the kiosk lifecycle. It does not -- nothing in the service allow-list, the /service-control POST, the splash hand-off or the systemd units moved; the diff is one pure export, a `hidden` write driven by the existing poll, one CSS rule and one markup attribute. Iris's reading (pure UI) holds.

stories.title: Polish P-3: DTC detail overlay hierarchy -- directive-first + carded sections + bigger Back
stories.completionNotes: ALL 4 ACs MET. THE FINDING IS THE STORY -- read this before anything else: `detailLine()` wraps EVERY row's text in a `.detail-value` span, and that span declared its OWN `font-size: 13px; color: var(--text-primary)`. A child's own declaration beats an inherited value NO MATTER how specific the parent selector is, so every size and colour the row classes declared was INERT on the rendered text. That means US-488's entire tier ramp on `.detail-directive` -- built one story ago, tested, shipped -- PAINTED NOTHING: a STOP directive rendered 13px text-primary, identical to a MINOR one. The caveat never rendered amber, the footer never rendered muted, `.dtc-fix-directive` never rendered bold amber. AC-1 ('larger') is literally unachievable without fixing it, so `.detail-value` is now `font-size: inherit; color: inherit` and every row class finally means what it says. GENERALIZABLE: a CSS test that asserts a PARENT rule's declaration proves the declaration EXISTS, never that it reaches the glyphs -- if the text lives in a child with its own rule, the parent loses. My guard asserts the child inherits, which is the only form that can catch this. AC-1: the band leads (ordering asserted on the real DOM builder, not intent), 18px/800 (guard demands a full step above base copy, not a token 1px bump), a padded slab with a `currentColor` left edge -- currentColor so the tier rules keep setting exactly ONE property and the accent can never disagree with the text beside it. THE OTHER JUDGEMENT CALL: AC-1's parenthetical says green 'keeps' SAFE TO CLEAR ONCE LOGGED -- but it never rendered. `codeDetailView` gated the band on `isStopWatch`, so MINOR and uncurated codes got NO band, while the takeover has shown both since US-405 and US-488 had already added (dead) CSS for both tiers. On the ONE screen the operator opens to ask 'what do I do', a blank answer reads as 'nothing to worry about' -- the dishonest answer on an uncurated code (F-1). Band now renders for every actionable tier; `na` ALONE stays blank ('not applicable to this vehicle' is a fact, not an instruction, it never alarms anywhere else, and the fix slot already says it) -- pinned by my guard AND by the pre-existing deploy-kit assertion. AC-2: one shared `.detail-card` shell (border + the scale) across freeze-frame, fix and the Clear zone -- three near-identical boxes drift the first time one is edited. The fix card's label was BRANCH-LOCAL inside `mode === 'fix'`, so a STOP/WATCH card rendered a bordered box with NO heading; it is now unconditional via a new `fixSectionLabel(mode)` export -- mode-driven because heading a diagnose directive 'SUGGESTED FIX' would undo S-4 in the label while the body still obeys it (fix->SUGGESTED FIX, directive->NEXT STEP, na->APPLICABILITY, unknown mode falls back to NEXT STEP never to SUGGESTED FIX). AC-3: `.detail-head` was a FIXED 36px around a 40px (--tap-min) Back button -- the one control that guarantees the operator is never trapped was overflowing its own header; now min-height 44px, and the button has a real edge (40px of transparent nothing is not a target you can SEE). One spacing scale (--detail-gap/--detail-gap-tight/--detail-pad) declared on #dtc-detail and consumed by the sections. AC-4 (presentation only) is not asserted by assurance but by 5 re-run guards: S-4 fix-replacement (raw suggestedFix still never surfaces on stop/watch), trust badge, all 5 clear-gate reasons, the chip/tier table, and the stop/watch directive wording. WALKED INTO THE US-490 TRAP FOR REAL: joining the card shell gave `#dtc-clear-zone` `display: flex`, which OUTRANKS the UA `[hidden]` rule -- so hiding the zone would have painted an empty labelled box anyway. `#dtc-clear-zone[hidden]{display:none}` stated explicitly, with a guard. (The zone hides with its button because an empty 'CLEAR CODES' card is a new visual regression; the GATE is untouched -- visibility still comes from clearButtonView() and the server re-checks on submit.) Also caught mid-flight: two of my own guards pointed at strings the refactor moved, and one regex window could have run past its branch and matched the OLD branch-local label -- both re-bounded by index slicing and watched red first. GREEN in-loop: 25 new pass; tests/ui/ + tests/deploy/test_dashboard_kit.py = 241 passed; tests/pi/splash/test_states_http_multi_assets.py green; ruff clean on the touched file. GATES for PM: `make` is not on this host's PATH (ran ruff directly); black+mypy not installed (standing gap); no config change so validate_config.py N/A; full suite is the PM integration gate (no base module touched -- dashboard dist + one new test file). PI-RUNTIME GATE OWED, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE STORY LOOKS: because the value-span fix un-freezes colours that have NEVER rendered, the whole detail overlay changes appearance at once. Confirm on the 480x320 panel -- a STOP detail's directive reads --critical-red at 18px and leads; a WATCH reads amber; a MINOR now shows a GREEN 'SAFE TO CLEAR ONCE LOGGED' band where there was none; an uncurated code shows an amber 'GET DIAGNOSED'; an `na` shows no band at all; the caveat line is amber and the footer/meta are muted (all first-time renders); the three cards are bordered + labelled and do not overflow at 480px; '‹ Back' is a visibly-bordered >=40px target inside a 44px header; and a no-clearable-codes detail shows NO clear card.
acceptance: directive-first for 🔴/🟡: the action band (REDUCE LOAD·PULL OVER / GET DIAGNOSED) moves directly under the code+chip hero, larger (🟢 keeps 'safe to clear once logged')
card the sections: freeze-frame/context, suggested-fix+trust-badge, and the Clear zone each become a bordered block with a small uppercase label
consistent spacing scale; the ‹ Back target >= 40px with clear affordance
